newsitem.title: POLAND: Poles unhappy with govt handling of flood - poll.
newsitem.headline: Poles unhappy with govt handling of flood - poll.

text.p: Poles are dissatisfied with the way the government handled the disastrous July floods in southwestern Poland but are more forgiving of local authorities, a poll by the public CBOS polling institute said.
The survey showed Poles were happy with the performance of fire brigades, police and the military in fighting the crisis.
But 43 percent of those not directly affected by the floods were dissatisfied with the work of the central authorities, 26 thought their work was good and 25 percent middling.
Of those directly affected by the calamity, 43 percent were unhappy about the central government's performance with 28 percent viewing it as good and 19 percent as average.
Local authorities received 36 percent "good", 27 percent "middling" and 28 percent "bad" marks.
Poland's worst floods for centuries killed 54 people and swamped huge areas of farmland.
